models.summary: A person splits a fixed money holding between traditional currency and digital currency. Utility is Cobb-Douglas in the two holdings, with exponents set by personal traits such as risk and liquidity preference. Preferences are normal, monotone and convex. A Lagrange multiplier gives the first-order conditions, and each holding comes out as a constant share of the total: the traditional share is alpha over alpha plus beta. The split is the micro foundation for the money demand used at the national level.

models.summary: At the national level, money demand is the sum of the two individual holdings and money supply is the sum of digital and traditional supply. Equilibrium sets real supply equal to demand, and demand splits into a transaction-and-precautionary part linear in income and a speculative part linear and falling in the interest rate. Solving gives the LM curve: the interest rate rises with income and with a fall in real money supply. Points above the curve mean too little money demand, points below mean too much. The curve flattens when money demand is more sensitive to the rate or less sensitive to income, and it shifts right when demand falls on its own or supply rises.

models.summary: The IS curve collects the interest-rate and output pairs that clear the home goods market. Income balances two ways, so broad investment equals broad saving. Investment falls with the rate and rises with net exports; saving rises with income and with the budget surplus. Equating them gives the rate as a straight line falling in output. The intercept carries autonomous spending, the budget deficit and net exports.
objectives: Express the goods-market interest rate as a function of output.

models.summary: The FE curve collects the interest-rate and output pairs that balance the payments. The current account is net exports and the financial account is net capital inflow, and external balance sets their sum to zero, so net exports equal net capital outflow. Imports rise with income and fall with the real exchange rate, exports are fixed, and net inflow rises as the foreign rate exceeds the home rate. Solving gives the home rate as a straight line rising in output. This is the curve the paper adds international capital flow parameters to, and it is the link between the real country and the virtual one.
